text: The passage repays a reader who attends to what is missing from it; and a silence in such a narrative signifies something of itself, and is more than a mere leaving out. Sarah appears nowhere in the chapter, and in the very next verse the book announces her death. The scene implies, though it never says so, that something in the household did not survive the mountain; and at precisely the point where a weaker story would dwell, the narrator turns away. Abraham returns to the servants, and of Isaac nothing is said.
